ara: quick note — saw a customer hit our soft-fallbacks during a capacity spike, but headers from gateway looked like they were ignored. can we confirm header precedence?

matt: which headers? X-Customer-Tier or the override header?

ara: looks like X-Route-Override was present, but route matcher still picked default lane. example payload snippet below. not sure if matcher is evaluating headers after path priority.

ara: ```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.com
X-Customer-Tier: enterprise
X-Route-Override: prefer-backup-model

{"prompt":"..."}
```

sophia: if X-Route-Override is intended as a runtime tie-breaker it should be applied in the matching phase before lane selection. currently code applies it as a post-match transform (oof).

devon: +1. we always talked about header precedence but tests never covered override headers + regex route collisions. feels like our matcher priority list is: exact path > path-regex > header, which is wrong for overrides.

nina: consequences: fallback chain used wrong backup model, increased latency and cost because it hit bigger model instead of quantized backup. single tenant SLA was affected.

matt: propose small change: add header-priority flag per route. default false. when true, header rules are evaluated at the same weight as path exact matches. config sketch:```
- route: /v1/generate
  priority: 10
  header_priority: true  # new
  match:
    - header: X-Route-Override: prefer-backup-model
    - path: ^/v1/generate$
  fallback:
    mode: soft  # allow degraded tokens instead of hard reject
    chain: [m-small-q3, m-small-q4, m-medium]
```

ara: i like header_priority. but can we avoid config explosion? maybe a global matcher policy with an allowlist of header keys that can elevate priority.

sophia: yes — global list: matcher.override_headers = ["X-Route-Override","X-Canary-Force"] and per-route opt-outs. safer.

devon: telemetry concern: we need to emit which part of the matcher caused selection so ops can debug. suggest a header in responses `X-Matcher-Decision: path|hdr|default` and an internal metric `matcher_decision_count{route,reason}`.

nina: add fallback lineage header too: `X-Fallback-Chain: m-small-q3->m-small-q4->m-medium` so the console can surface exact chain used.

matt: agree. also circuit-breaker trigger needs to attach reason 'capacity' or 'latency' so that fallback is explanatory. eg `cb.reason=capacity_spike` in traces.

ara: UX ask — can console show a per-route table with columns: current lane, last_fallback_chain, fallback_rate_1h, avg_latency_before_fallback? this would help SREs triage.

sophia: Rollouts: for canary we should default to soft fallback (no hard reject) and expose an opt-in hard-cb flag per rollout. otherwise customers get opaque 503s.

devon: implementation plan:
- matcher: evaluate override headers at match-time if matcher.override_headers contains key (PR #2791)
- telemetry: emit matcher_decision and X-Fallback-Chain (PR #2792)
- console: add fallback_rate and last_chain panel (dashboard ticket INF-412)

matt: i'll take PR #2791, will add unit tests for header+path collisions.

nina: i'll own the telemetry piece, will add metric names and sample dashboards.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: staging build 2026-03-18T18:10:00Z for branch feature/matcher-override (dry run)

ara: thanks — milestone: get header-precedence in staging, validate with synthetic spike, then flip global matcher override flag for a small set of routes.

matt: ETA for staging PR: today EOD. follow-up sync if staging shows mismatch. :thumbsup:
